issues.detail: The constant DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16 is now declared in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat instead of being imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat as before. Two copies of the same magic number in adjacent format classes is exactly the kind of duplication that drifts. Either keep the static import from the canonical home or add a one-line comment saying it must equal the flat format's value. The data here is a single number with a single meaning; give it one home.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throwing UOE is a runtime check where the type system could speak
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.fieldsWriter and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.fieldsWriter now throw UnsupportedOperationException. The codebase pattern for backward codecs already established for prior formats appears to be the same, so this is consistent, but the data flow says 'read-only format' and the type does not. A ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat base or a tagged read-only marker would make the shape obvious at compile time. Acceptable to leave for consistency, but worth noting as an accumulated pattern smell across the backward_codecs tree.

issues.description: Test-only RW subclasses proliferating (V0, V1, plain RW) without a clear taxonomy
issues.detail: We now have Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat, Lucene99RWV0HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat, and Lucene99RWV1HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat. The naming carries version semantics that aren't documented anywhere central. A single javadoc paragraph in package-info (or a README in the test package) explaining what V0 vs V1 represents would prevent the next contributor from adding V2 without understanding the shape. Small thing; the data structure of test fixtures has a story and nobody is telling it.

issues.description: Visibility downgrade from protected to package-private fields on abstract class
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues changed protected fields to package-private. This is correct for the move (subclasses are now all in the same package), and matches the goal of making the abstract surface smaller. Worth a one-line confirmation that no external subclasses existed; given @lucene.experimental and the move to backward_codecs, this is fine. Noting for completeness.

review.summary: This is a straightforward physical move: legacy Lucene99 scalar-quantized format classes relocate from core to backward_codecs, with writers gutted to throw UnsupportedOperationException and test-only RW subclasses providing write capability for round-trip tests. The data shape is right — a read-only format in the legacy module plus narrowly-scoped RW test helpers — and the visibility tightening (public to package-private NAME, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, reader constructor) reflects the smaller surface. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE on the whole, with two minor smells: a duplicated DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant that used to be imported from the flat format, and a growing V0/V1 RW-subclass family that needs one paragraph of documentation before someone adds a V2. No blockers; merge-ready after a quick decision on the constant duplication.
